Nineteenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 2004 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication No. 17, pp 189-221 
Environmental Status at Indian Polar Research
Station Maitri-A Comprehensive Study
Anoop Kumar Tiwari and Sunil Kulkarni
National Environmental Engineering Research Institute, Nagpur
Abstract
A comprehensive study of the different environmental components viz. air, water,
land, noise was undertaken during the austral summer of 1999-2000 at the Indian Polar
Research Station Maitri, in compliance with the statutory requirements of the Antarctic
Treaty. The first objective of the study was to assess the impacts of various scientific
programs and their associated logistic support facilities on the fragile ecosystem of Antarctica.
The second objective was to establish India's first Environmental Monitoring Laboratory
on a permanent basi s in Antarctica. Identification of major sources of pollution and
quantification of pollution load was carried out through an extensive environmental
monitoring program spread over a period of 30-40 days. Preliminary studies reveal that the
levels of pollution are not alarming but there is scope for concern looking into the critical
aspects of Antarctic environment and the carrying capacity of the environment surrounding
Maitri station. Based on the findings an Environmental Management Plan has been
formulated with recourse to sustainable development at Maitri station.
Introduction
The Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty
which was adopted in 1991 by the Antarctic Treaty nations provides for the
comprehensive protection of the Antarctic environment, and sets out tightly
drawn rules governing human activities there. The Protocol on Environmental
Protection defines Antarctica as a "natural reserve devoted to peace and
science." Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was first adopted by
the Antarctic Treaty Consultative Parties (ATCPs) in 1987, when
recommendation XIV-2 was agreed upon at the XIV Antarctic Treaty
Consultative Meetings (ATCM). A set of procedural guidelines were
developed to be used by national Antarctic organizations for evaluation of
the impact of scientific activities and their associated logistic support facilities
on the fragile environment of Antarctica. The protocol on environmental
protection to the Antarctic Treaty which has been agreed to by 26 ATCPs
(including India) in 1991 requires EIA to be applied in the planning and

operation of all activities undertaken in Antarctica. A logical structure of
assessment has been set up, where every activity, even  simple activities
like building a small field camp, are subject to a "Preliminary Assessment".
If environmental questions arise then an "Initial Environmental Evaluation"
is done. The highest level of assessment, reserved for projects like airstrip
construction is called a "Comprehensive Environmental Evaluation".
Plate 1: Ambient Air Quality Monitoring in Progress at one of the 
Locations around Maitri station, Antarctica 
In view of the guidelines imposed under the Environmental Protocol
of Antarctic Treaty, the National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research
(NCAOR), Department of Ocean Development (DOD) r etained National
Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI), Nagpur for
conducting a detailed impact assessment of the different scientific and logistic
activities on the pristine environment surrounding Maitri station and to prepare
an effective Environmental Management Plan (EMP). One of the
mandatory requirements of the Antarctic Treaty is that all countries
maintaining a permanent polar research stations in Antarctica should have
a permanent environmental monitoring laboratory at that station for carrying
out year-round environmental assessment. This important project of setting
up India's first permanent environmental monitoring  laboratory at Maitri
(Plate 2) was also successfully executed by NEERI during the 19th expedition.
The project included installation of various instruments such as conductivity
meter, spectrophotometer, pH meter, distilled-water unit, heating mantles,
oven, incubator, hot-plate, etc. All the instruments were properly calibrated

Infrastructure of Maitri Station
Site: Maitri station is located in the Schirmacher Oasis at 70°45' 53"S
latitude and 11°44' 03"E longitude. It is built on an ice-free rocky moraine
at an elevation of 117m above mean sea level.
Engineering support: Maitri is India's indigenously designed polar research
